title: S-1000-48 1000W, 21A, 48V DC Power Supply
description: Connect this unit to 110 or 220 Volts AC household power, and it will supply 1000 Watts at 48 Volts DC and 21 Amps. If more than 21 Amps is required, please search Amazon for "AmpFlow parallelable power supply"This power supply has been engineered for use with DC motors. Most power supplies designed for use with LED lighting or other electronics will simply shut down when exposed to the high current demands of motors. Built-in current limiting protects the unit from overloads and short circuits. The current limiting feature enables these power supplies to keep functioning through the high-current start-up surges from motors. Current is limited to the rated maximum even when a larger load is called for, (like when a DC motor starts up). Also, inductive loads (like motors) can cause damage to power supplies that are not designed for them.These power supplies also work well in any application where AC line voltage needs to be converted to DC voltage. Other uses include LEDs, HAM radio, and battery charging.Short-circuit and overload protections help these units survive harsh operating conditions. The power supply shuts down temporarily if the temperature, current, or voltage goes beyond the safe operating range, and it starts up again automatically when the condition goes away – no rebooting is necessary.This high-efficiency power supply has an output voltage that is adjustable by plus or minus 10%. It includes an EMI filter to minimize interference with radio signals and a soft-start circuit that reduces the AC inrush current peaks. Every power supply goes through a full-load burn-in test, so no defective unit leaves the factory. This unit meets all the following safety and EMC standards:UL 1950, EN60950, IEC100-3-2, CE, ROHSAmpFlow® power supplies are available in 5V, 12V, 24V, 36V, and 48 Volts at up to 1000 Watts. Search Amazon for "AmpFlow power supply" for more choices.

top_review: Over the years I have owned iPads I have tried out a good number of cases. Some were just junk. Some didn’t fit even though the manufacturer listed my iPad model as fitting. Some had awful materials. Others just looked plain ugly even if protective. This case is made exactly the same as the last one I owned which was on an iPad 5th generation. It has a cute design, has a flexible and protective interior to put the iPad into (without struggling to get it in or out) and the iPad STAYS in. No corners coming out when you pick it up or use it. It has a magnetic closure that turns the iPad off when closing the cover, and is great at standing your iPad up at an angle on your lap or table. It doesn’t have a holder for the pen, or any access to attach a keyboard. (You would have to remove it) I own neither so that is not an issue for me. I can’t stress enough how nice this will keep your iPad. As I said the last case I had was made exactly the same way, and when I took my iPad out to trade it in the Apple store sales woman commented on how it was like new out of the box. If you only like your iPad with nothing on it, this isn’t for you. If you want a really sturdy cover, this is it. In so far as the design on the cover I have no idea how it would hold up rubbing up against something else in a pack or purse constantly. It seems pretty well made to me unless you are someone who abuses your electronic devices. (I’m talking about you people with cracked screens on phones, etc because you dropped it flat out on the cement from several feet) I do not use a computer, laptop or otherwise. I live on my iPad at least 6 hours a day so I want it protected. This is like a cute little thin book. Oh - and all the holes line up exactly where they are supposed to. I consider this a very good value for the money. And I’m picky.

Lens filters improve photographs by giving photographers control over light and allowing them to emphasize the features of a scene that they consider most important.This filter kit is a combination of the three essential filters no photographer should be without.UV--Film and a digital CCD are more sensitive to UV light than our eyes are. This filter will remove the UV light and more importantly protect your lens from moisture, scratches, and damage.Polarizer--provides color and contrast enhancement. top_review: This walnut wood and matte black iron headphone stand is truly impressive, featuring a stunning combination of materials that gives it a modern aesthetic, perfect for pairing with high-end audio gear. Its sturdy construction and 10.2" height comfortably accommodate large heavy headphones, such as the 730 g HEDDphone ONE, and just fits the taller Hifiman models with asymmetrical ovoid ear cups.However, I did notice that the Hifiman HE1000 series and other brands with headbands wider than 60mm do not fit between the wood trim pieces of the metal rest as was stated in the ad. I found a workaround by removing the rear trim piece, which allowed me to accommodate the HE1000 headband while still maintaining the aesthetic appeal of the front trim.The addition of non-slip silicone pads is a thoughtful feature, ensuring that the stand remains securely in place and protects my wood desktop from scratches. I also appreciate the integrated phone slots for both vertical and horizontal positioning, which add everyday convenience without detracting from the stand’s clean design. The walnut trim on the headband rest not only prevents slippage but also adds a subtle, elegant accent.The packaging was impressive, with the contents secured inside a protective Styrofoam container, and the wooden base further protected in a plastic bag. Assembly was straightforward, thanks to the easy-to-follow two-step instructions and the included Phillips-head screwdriver, along with extra screws provided.While the installation of the machine screws was simple, I did encounter some issues. The wood base did not have pilot holes to center the wood screws for installation, but it was easy enough to create a pilot hole using an ice pick or nail. A more serious issue is that the wood screw heads are not countersunk into the metal post base plate, and the post base is not sufficiently recessed into the wood base, which means the screw heads protrude very slightly above the wood surface. Without the silicone pads, this could potentially scratch tabletops.Additionally, there are a few small rough spots on the wood base that could have been better sanded down, and the steel headphone rest has some rough exposed spot welds and unusual crescent-shaped holes along the edges.Overall, despite these minor blemishes and the slightly protruding wood screw heads, this stand feels luxurious and offers great value. I highly recommend it if you’re in the market for a new headphone stand.

top_review: After reading several reviews both on Amazon and elsewhere, I deceided to purchase this TV. I was a little worried about having a TV of this size mailed / delivered to my house. My fears were unjustified. I scheduled the delivery through Amazon and everything went as planned. The delivery showed up at the exact time they said it would. Two Amazon employees had it off the truck and in my living room within a matter of minutes. The box was in perfect shape and showed that it had been handled with care. There were no holes, tears, dents, or rattles inside.It took about an hour to mount the TV on my living room wall. The setup was quick and easy. Samsung really made it simple with onscreen prompts. The picture is beautiful just using the factory settings. I downsized to this 65" screen from a Viseo 70" TV. Can hardly tell the difference in size. I chose not to upgrade to the 75" Samsung model because I could not justify spending an additional $900.00 for 10 more inches.The TV processor is fast. The apps come up quickly and scrolling through is smooth and seamless. The remote is great. Seems minimal at first but it has everything that is needed without lots of distracting buttons.I have no complaints with this TV. I paired this with a small soundbar from Samsung (T-400), again had everything connected in minutes. The built in TV speakers sounded great and would have been perfect for a smaller room. I highly reccomend this TV for anyone looking for a QLED display. Be sure to stick with the Q-80 series of this model, you get a lot of features for only a little more than the Q-60 or Q-70 series.UPDATE 11/4/21I have had this TV for 6 months with no issues. The only thing I can complain about is that the remote has a built in battery that can't be replaced. It is designed to be charged by the photo cell on the back so you must get use to storing the remote with the photo cell up. It also has and input connector to charge via USB cable. I purchased the cable and the remote charges quickly. Would have been nice if the cable came with the remote! Definitly buy the cable, it should only cost a few dollars on Amazon.My TV came with a protective film on the screen. It was obvious that it need to be removed before using. Not sure why there are so many issues with this.I am very happy with this TV. It has worked out well for me and my family.

top_review: The aluminum alloy feels super sturdy right out of the box, not that cheap soft metal that dents if you look at it wrong. Once I slid it into the track and tightened it down, it locked in place like it was welded on there. The install was super quick. I loosened the T bolt, slid it into the YakAttack style track on my kayak, and tightened it up with just a couple turns. No wobble, no shifting, even when I leaned on it by accident climbing back in the kayak. The ball itself is smooth and the coating feels tough. My RAM C size arm clamps onto it without slipping, even when I crank the arm down a bit crooked like I sometimes do when I’m in a hurry.  I mounted my fish finder on it first and took it out on a windy morning. The water was choppy and I was bouncing around more than I wanted, but the mount didn’t move at all. The screen stayed right where I set it. No sagging, no slow drifting downward like I’ve had with other mounts. I even smacked it with my paddle once and it didn’t budge. I thought for sure I knocked it loose but nope, still tight.One thing I liked a lot is how easy it is to adjust the position. I loosened the arm, swung the fish finder over to the side, and tightened it again without the ball slipping. The bigger 1.5 inch ball makes a huge diff for heavier gear. I also tried it with a rod holder just to see how it handled the weight and it held up great. I tugged on the rod holder a bit and the base didn’t twist or shift in the track. The T bolt is solid too. It doesn’t strip or feel soft when tightening. I’ve had some mounts where the bolt feels like it’s made of butter, but this one feels like it can take some abuse. The base sits flat in the track and doesn’t rock side to side. I checked it after a few hours on the water and it was still tight.I also used it in the back of my truck on a short rail section I have for mounting gear. It fit the track fine and held a camera arm steady while I was messing around with some filming. The ball didn’t loosen even with the truck bouncing around on a gravel road. The aluminum alloy seems like it’ll hold up long term without corroding or getting that chalky look some cheaper mounts get.

top_review: It is not often that I find a patch cable that can actually MARGINALLY PASS using the TIA Patch Cord Test on a Fluke Versiv DSX-8000.  I have yet to find one that will fully PASS, regardless of manufacturer, so I am not dinging the marginal pass.  This Cat6 shielded cord does indeed MARGINAL PASS with PCA adapters.  On a TIA Cat6 Channel test, using CHA adapters and looser testing criteria, this patch cord fully PASSES.  A further test was conducted, using 10GBASE-T + 802.3bt, which is 10 Gigabit and a powerful variation of PoE.  PASS was the result.  So, in summation, here are results:T568 Cat6 Patch Cord Test, PCA to PCA:  MARGINAL PASS -- This test also takes the terminations into accountT568 Cat6 Channel Test, CHA to CHA:  PASS -- This test does NOT measure terminations, and only the cableApplication Test, 10GBASE-T + 802.3bt:  PASS -- This test is a practical snap shot of "on the ground" performanceIt should be noted that other patch cords, from other manufacturers, will FAIL T568 Patch Cord testing and may not even pass the Channel test.  There is a lot of garbage cable out there.  Buyer beware.I am a Fluke Networks Certified Network Technician, and am trained and registered to provide DSX test results.  The Certification tester in question, and the accessories used, will set you back north of $13K, so hopefully my weighing in will add some value to your decision as most folks have no ability to afford one of these test setups and do not have the ability to obtain the training necessary to use one in any case.The one MINOR thing I dislike is the boot design of the cable.  It is the half moon variety, which dries out over time and becomes stiff and difficult to disconnect cables if it gets in the way.  I prefer other boot types.  I will not remove a star for this.  I will often cut the half moon boot off with flush cutters so it does not become an issue.

description: The STR-A7III-RIG is a new form-fitting camera cage direct from Ikan. The frame is shaped to accommodate the Alpha a7 III and a7R III camera bodies. The cage comes in three main parts: the top handle, the base, and the camera frame. The top handle mounts directly to the front of the cage frame. There are 42 1/4-20 mounts on the top handle when it is bare, but the grip can be covered with Ikan grips or, if custom grips are needed, can fit most bicycle handles. A 15mm rod can also be inserted into the end of the handle and held in place with a 1/4-20 screw through one of the many mounts. a cold shoe mount is located at the front of the handle, near where it connects to the frame's front. There are multiple mounting holes on the front of the frame for positioning the handle to either side to make room for accessories and audio adapters. The base is simple and sleek, with mounts for two included 15mm rods (2x 200mm rods plus 2x 100mm extensions w/ couplings) and both 1/4-20 and 3/8-16 mounting points for tripod quick release plates. The locking knobs are large and solid, and have a kipping function that allows tightening even when the knobs are partially obstructed. The base locks to the frame with an Arca-Swiss style connection, and there are hard stops on either side to allow safe horizontal positioning. This base also has vertically position able rods that have about 1" of play to better accommodate matte boxes, follow focuses, and lens supports to many styles of lens. There is a lock and track on the very bottom of the base for lightweight (15mm) dovetail plates, but note that not all dovetail plates conform to the same standard of size or manufacturing tolerances.

top_review: Auto focus is fast and accurate, image quality is quite good, especially for this price. Nice and sharp and the size and ease of use is unbeatable. This is about as close as I can get my Fujifilm X-T5 to feeling like an X100VI, fantastic for street photos (if this focal length works for you). I usually shoot with a 23mm and this is a bit tighter, but worth the tradeoff.2 MONTH UPDATE:I find myself leaving this on my camera and just shooting with this. Somehow, my eye isn't used to seeing this focal length yet, and that's something I really like about it. It's hard to believe how good this is considering how freaking tiny this lens is. It's easy to forget to flip the lens cap away, but it is, by far, my favorite and most convenient lens as a result of this little feature. CA and defraction just aren't much of an issue at all, or at least not noticeable to me. Weight is just non-existent. There's just not much to say about this - it's really good! Still a big fan, and I think I appreciate it because I want to take my camera out and about even more frequently than I used to.

description: 6 foot AC Cord, Figure 8 Polarized When comparing with other cords, please keep in mind: The figure-8 connector is POLARIZED (it has a 'corner'), this ensures proper Live/Neutral polarity in your appliance. Please see images and compare to your existing cord or appliance 1.) This is a non-integral cord. Most cheaper "competitors" are integral (see the difference below) 2.) This is a 6 foot long cord 3.) This is a 10 AMP cord, meaning it can carry up to 10 Amps at 125 volts. Most other cords are only rated up to 7 amps. 4.) This cord is UL (Underwriter Laboratories) listed 5.) This cord is rated to 105 degrees C (220 F) A non-integral cord (which is what we're selling) is a cord where the conductors are double-insulated: There is the inner insulation which wraps around each conductor individually, and then there's another thick layer (the outer black layer you actually see). This non-integral (double-insulated) cord is stronger and more reliable than an integral (single-insulated) cord because it provides additional strength and protection for ultimate durability and safety. To check if a cord is double-insulated (non-integral) like ours, feel the flat portion of the cord with your fingers: If there is a groove running down the center of the cords (usually on both sides), then that's a good sign that the cord is only single-insulated.

description: Product description Excellent cosmetic condition, shows very little use. Battery door works fine as does the entire camera. Will ship with new, factory sealed battery, non-original case and starter CF card. Amazon.com With the Coolpix 880, Nikon has taken the 3.3-megapixel CCD and many of the advanced features from its semiprofessional 990 model and put them into a traditional compact point-and-shoot design simple enough for anyone to use.The Nikkor all-glass lens features a 2.5x optical zoom (equivalent to 38- 95mm on a 35mm camera) with a macro mode that focuses down to 1.6 inches. A 4x digital zoom further increases magnification at lower resolutions. Images are stored on a Type I CompactFlash card (8 MB card included). Maximum image resolution is 2,048 x 1,536 pixels, and an uncompressed TIFF mode is available (remember, however, that uncompressed images are so large that you'll need a bigger memory card to store even one full-resolution uncompressed image).Though the camera defaults to full-auto point-and-shoot mode, it has a host of manual features for advanced photographers. In addition, Nikon has included 11 special modes in which the camera is automatically programmed with the appropriate settings for specific situations like sunsets, beaches, night portraits, and extreme close-ups. For example, switch the camera to its party/indoor setting, and it will slow down the shutter and use a slow-synch flash with red-eye reduction.The 880 is Nikon's smallest digital camera, with overall dimensions of only 3.9 by 3 by 2.1 inches, and weighs only 9.7 ounces without a battery.Power is provided by either a disposable 2CR5 lithium battery (included) or an optional rechargeable lithium-ion battery. For environmental and economic reasons, we strongly recommend getting the rechargeable battery kit for anything more than occasional use.Image transfer is quick and easy with the included USB cable. If you have an older computer with only a serial port, the Coolpix 880 also supports serial image transfer (though you'll need to purchase the serial cable separately). The camera ships with an impressive software suite that includes Genuine Fractals 2.0 LE for file compression and scaling, Cumulus 5.0 demo for image management, and Great Photo! for image manipulation and correction.

top_review: I’ve been traveling with the WANDRD Transit Travel Backpack 45L and it has become my favorite travel pack, beating out comparable bags I own from Osprey, Thule in day‑to‑day use.​Organization and pockets (the big win)What makes this pack stand out is the complexity of the organization in a good way. As someone who carries a laptop, tablet, chargers, and assorted tech with chocolate, the number and layout of pockets is exactly what I wanted.Multiple quick‑access pockets on the outside mean I can grab headphones, tickets, or a power bank without digging through the main compartment.The dedicated laptop and tech areas are well padded and separated, so I can slide devices out easily on a crowded train without opening everything up.​Compared with my competitor travel packs, which are more “big clamshell plus a few pockets,” the Wandrd Transit feels designed around digital gear from the start, not as an afterthought.​If you find “lots of zippers and compartments” confusing, this bag is not for you. But if you like having specific homes for earbuds, cables, all other, and water, this is a major upgrade.Train travel and mobilityFor train‑based travel, this has been excellent:The 40(+5)L size is large enough for multi‑day or multi‑week trips, but still manageable in overhead racks and under seats on most trains.​Side and top handles, plus the way the bag holds its structure, make it easy to lift into luggage racks quickly, without straps tangling everywhere.​Walking between stations and platforms, the harness is comfortable. It’s heavier than an Osprey or Thule pack of the same volume, but the padding, load lifters, and sternum strap keep it controlled and stable.Build quality is where this feels closer to “camera bag” than standard travel backpack:The tarpaulin‑style exterior and YKK zippers feel extremely robust and provide better weather resistance.​The overall construction is confidence‑inspiring: thick materials, reinforced grab points, and hardware that feels premium.Compared with my other brands:Osprey: Lighter and more hiking‑oriented comfort, but less weather‑resistant and with simpler organization for tech. Transit wins for digital gear and bad weather; Osprey still wins for pure carry comfort on very long walks.​Thule: The Subterra‑style pack is sleek and well built, but has fewer pockets and less “granular” organization; WANDRD is better if you carry lots of small tech accessories.​Amazon Basics: Those packs are great for the price, but the materials and stitching are clearly a budget tier. The zipper ties lock with each other, so it's a nice confidence feature.Internal organization for chargers, cables, and drives keeps everything separated—no more cable spaghetti at the bottom of the bag.Lockable zippers and the way some pockets are tucked against the back panel make it harder for casual pickpockets to access critical gear in crowded stations and cars.​With other packs, I often had to choose between “tech safe but buried” or “tech accessible but not secure.” This bag finally gets that balance right for my use.Comfort is very good for a travel‑oriented pack:Thick, well‑shaped shoulder straps and a padded back panel distribute weight well.Load lifters and sternum strap help a lot when fully loaded with electronics and clothes.There’s an optional hip belt (sold separately) if you really overload it; I found it comfortable even without the belt for typical train travel loads.​The main trade‑offs:It is heavier than simpler 40L packs from Osprey or Thule.The “crumply” look when partially packed and the large number of zippers/pockets won’t appeal to minimalists.​For me, those are acceptable trade‑offs for the protection and organization I get.Bottom line: If your travel looks like mine, lots of trains, lots of digital equipment, and a preference for complex pocket layouts that keep everything exactly where you want it—the WANDRD Transit Travel Backpack 45L is an outstanding choice and, in practice, more functional than my comparable bags from Osprey and Thule. description: Years ago I heard author Barry Lopez give a reading at the Tattered Cover Bookstore in Denver. That evening he wore a faded red oxford shirt, Levis, boots, a glove leather belt with a turquoise-studded buckle, and a brown messenger bag on his shoulder. Lopez is not an overpowering man, and it was clear he’d made the choice for a bag that wasn’t either. He carried himself with that manly confidence that doesn’t need to show-off.
